Then the dentist forms a treatment plan based on where the patient believes the pain is coming from

title: Patient issues the dentist should be aware of before starting treatment include: a. history of allergies and any adverse effects from drugs formally or presently taken b. presence of prosthetic valves, joints, stents, pacemakers c. whether antibiotics should be administered prophylactically d. that the patient clots normally e. can have anesthetic with vasoconstrictor f. prone to emergencies like congestive heart failure

Typical prophylactic dosage of antibiotics prior to treatment includea. a. 2000 mg of penicillin or amoxicillin one hour prior to treatment b. 600 mg of clindamycin one hour prior to treatment c. 1000 mg of penicillin or amoxicillin at the time of the procedure d. 400 mg clindamycin one hour prior to the procedure e.  penicillin or amoxicillin as the choice over clindamycin when no allergies exist
Include all signs of hypoglycemia: a. confusion b. tremors c. agitation d. diaphoresis (sweating) e. tachycardia f. peripheral numbness in the hands and legs

Prior to giving opioid analgesics to a patient it is important to: a. determine whether or not they are taking drugs that could negatively interact with the narcotics you are prescribing b. that you make sure they take enough that they feel no pain post-operatively c. make a psychological evaluation of the patient to the best of your ability and if you have doubts talk to the patient’s physician d. prescribe on an as need basis determined by the patient
